decision: Plan drafted per operator directive 2026-06-12: audit-harness hygiene BEFORE integration-actions or any new product feature - the two follow-ups share the trust boundary that just produced a real hollow verdict (PR #46). One small plan, two features (writer sanitization, append-only iterations), both in completion_dispatch's writer seam.
rationale: Tighten the audit substrate while the failure is fresh; same boundary, one worktree.

decision: Path fields on the transcript (transcript_path/envelope_path) persist in PLACEHOLDERED form; the writer recomputes real output paths from plan_dir/auditor/iteration. Tests and any tooling must derive disk locations from the plan dir, not un-placeholder the recorded strings (username can appear in tmp paths outside $HOME, e.g. pytest-of-<user>, making reversal impossible).
rationale: Sanitization must cover path fields too (they leaked the home dir + username); making them informational-only keeps one canonical path-derivation seam and avoids a reversible-encoding trap.

decision: Audit iteration 1 (agree, 0 findings) judged HOLLOW by the PR #46 standard: transcript shows zero evidence reads - codex's read root was scripts/ because the CLI was invoked from there (DispatchTask.cwd=None inherits invoker cwd), so plan evidence was unreachable. ONE justified re-audit authorized from the worktree root so the transcript can prove reads. Precedent: 2026-06-11-001 D014/D015 remediation pattern. Side effect: re-audit live-demonstrates F002 (audit-codex-2.json appended, iteration 1 preserved byte-identical by the new writer).
rationale: Accepting a hollow agree on the hollow-verdict-fix plan would defeat the plan's purpose; cause is environmental (invoker cwd), not auditor misbehavior. Follow-up noted: dispatch seam should pin cwd to repo root rather than inherit.

decision: Re-audit iteration 2: codex agree, fully grounded (transcript shows reads of all four evidence artifacts, the test file, and both modules - the hollow-verdict standard is met). One overlay (severity higher): no artifact covered latest-reader behavior in a mixed-auditor directory. Remediated same-pass via TDD: _load_latest_audit_envelope(plan_dir, auditor=None) - auditor given selects that auditor's highest iteration; None preserves global-highest for the completed-plan backstop (sole production caller), which must tolerate historical auditor switches. New test pins both. Iteration 1 preserved byte-identical (sha256 cb36788c...) - F002 demonstrated live by the re-audit itself.
rationale: Per-auditor iteration numbering (F002) makes a stale foreign envelope able to carry a higher number than the current auditor's newest verdict; the reader needed a per-auditor selection seam to honour the acceptance's 'highest iteration for the auditor'.
